panels.title: Wall Power
panels.description: Measured at the socket, so it includes PSU losses and the monitor if it shares the plug.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Includes the ZFS ARC, which the kernel does not count as available but gives back under pressure.

panels.title: CPU Temp
panels.description: Tctl; the 7800X3D throttles at 89 °C.

panels.title: GPU Hotspot
panels.description: Junction limit is 110 °C.

panels.title: Hottest DIMM
panels.description: Keep below 60 °C. At 72 °C this kit corrupts data under sustained load (2026-10-09); fan-control ramps the case fans from 50 °C to full at 62 °C.

panels.title: Case Fans
panels.description: Duty fan-control commands on every header (35 % floor).

panels.title: Reboots in Range
panels.description: Boots inside the selected time range. Every one is also a dashed marker on the graphs; an unplanned one is a hang or reset, so cross-check `journalctl --list-boots`.

panels.title: Idle Floor (7 d)
panels.description: The lowest 5 % of wall readings over the last week: what the box draws doing nothing. The number to watch when tuning idle power.

panels.title: DIMM > 60 °C
panels.description: Time in the selected range the hottest DIMM spent above 60 °C. Should stay at zero.

panels.title: Clock Error
panels.description: chrony's estimate of how far the system clock is from true time, either direction. The Stability row has the history and the drift rate.

panels.title: Humidity
panels.description: 40-60 % is the comfortable band; above 60 % for long stretches is where mould starts.

panels.title: DIMMs vs Case Fans
panels.description: The DIMMs are the part that fails first here. fan-control (hosts/orchid/system/fan-control.nix) drives every case fan from the hotter DIMM (50 → 62 °C) or the CPU (65 → 88 °C), whichever asks for more. Fans on the right axis.

panels.title: Heat Above Room
panels.description: Each component minus the room temperature, so a hot afternoon doesn't look like a cooling problem. A rise here at the same load, over weeks, is dust or a drying paste.

panels.title: Fan Speeds
panels.description: Measured speed of every header with a fan on it. The GPU's own fans aren't here: its tach reads 0 under amdgpu, see the GPU row.

panels.title: Peak Temperatures in Range
panels.description: The hottest each part got in the selected range, coloured against its own limit: CPU throttles at 89, GPU hotspot 110, GPU memory ~105, DIMMs fail past ~65, SSDs throttle at ~80.

panels.title: Energy in Range
panels.description: Mean wall power over the selected range × its length. Gaps where the plug didn't answer are left out of the mean, not counted as 0 W.

panels.title: Where the Watts Go
panels.description: GPU and CPU as they report themselves, and the rest of the wall reading: board, DIMMs, SSDs, fans, the iGPU, PSU conversion loss and anything else on the same plug. The stack adds up to the wall line.

panels.title: Energy per Day
panels.description: Last 30 days, from the mean wall power of each day × 24 h. Each bar sits at the end of the day it covers.

panels.title: Uptime (30 d)
panels.description: Each drop to zero is a boot; a gap before it is time the box was dead (a hang, then a power-cycle). A planned reboot has no gap.

panels.title: Pressure Stall
panels.description: Share of wall time at least one task waited on the resource: how much the machine felt slow, whatever the cause. Memory 'all stalled' near 100 % is swap death, the one software failure that looks like a hang.

panels.title: Clock
panels.description: Whether chrony has the clock synchronised to network time: the kernel's max error is under 16 s, the same test timedatectl uses.

panels.title: Clock Error
panels.description: Estimated error is chrony's best guess at how far the clock is from true time. Max error is its worst-case bound (mostly half the round-trip delay to the servers); it grows while no sync arrives and drops back on each one. The kernel's own offset field is always 0 under chrony, which slews by frequency instead.

panels.title: Clock Drift
panels.description: How hard the kernel is speeding up (positive) or slowing down (negative) the clock to keep it on network time: the crystal's own drift, which moves with temperature. 10 ppm is ~0.9 s/day the clock would gain or lose without sync.

panels.title: Busiest Core vs Average
panels.description: A busiest core near 100 % with a low average is a single-threaded bottleneck: more cores won't help, clocks will.

panels.title: Temperature & Clock
panels.description: Tctl throttles at 89. Boost is ~5.0 GHz single core.

panels.title: Load Average
panels.description: 16 threads: sustained load above 16 means work is queueing.

panels.title: Package Power
panels.description: RAPL. The kernel makes energy_uj root-only; strata-exporter.nix chmods it at boot, and without that this panel is empty.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: Hotspot limit is 110 °C. ~24 °C over edge during steady load, 30-33 °C for the seconds it draws its full cap.

panels.title: Hotspot − Edge
panels.description: A delta that is high at moderate power, or that climbs over weeks, is paste or mount. Short spikes during power bursts are thermal lag and normal.

panels.title: Power vs Cap
panels.description: The cap (297 W, set by LACT in hosts/orchid/hardware.nix; stock 330 W) is the only thermal lever: the fans are already at 100 % under sustained load.

panels.title: Fan Duty
panels.description: Commanded duty, not a measured speed: this card's tach reads 0 RPM under amdgpu. Zero-RPM mode is on, so 0 at idle is expected.

panels.title: Core Voltage
panels.description: Stock: the offset is 0 mV since 2026-10-09 and stays there.

panels.title: Where the RAM Goes
panels.description: Programs is what's actually claimed. The ZFS cache (ARC, capped at 16 GiB) and page cache are reclaimable, so a full stack is not memory pressure; the PSI panel above is the honest signal.

panels.title: Swap Activity
panels.description: Pages per second. Brief blips are fine; sustained traffic means the working set doesn't fit.

panels.title: ZFS Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Share of ZFS reads served from RAM. Low while something cold is read (a game load, a model) and high again after.

panels.title: Major Page Faults
panels.description: Faults that had to read from disk. Spikes when programs start; a sustained rate is memory pressure.

panels.title: Busy Time
panels.description: Share of time each drive had I/O in flight. NVMe handles many requests at once, so 100 % here is not saturation, but sustained 100 % with high pressure-stall IO is.

panels.title: Temperature
panels.description: A wall or window colder than the dew point gets condensation.

panels.title: Humidity
panels.description: Absolute humidity doesn't move with temperature, so it shows whether airing actually removed moisture (right axis).

panels.title: Model
panels.description: Empty while the server is down.

panels.title: Live t/s
panels.description: Generation rate over the last ~2 s; 0 while idle.

panels.title: Experts in VRAM
panels.description: More cached experts = faster generation.

panels.title: Generation Speed
panels.description: tokens/s while generating. Live is a ~2 s window; request mean is since the request's first token; last request is the engine's own figure.

panels.title: Energy per Generated Mtoken
panels.description: Measured wall power divided by Strata's wall-clock generation rate over the last minute. Wall clock includes prefill and the idle gaps between an agent's turns. Only drawn while generating more than 5 t/s.

panels.title: Context & Reply Length
panels.description: A reply that climbs to 16384 is one that hit the output cap (a thinking spiral).

panels.title: Power Meter
panels.description: Offline with 'Authentication failed' in `journalctl -u tapo-exporter` means /persist/secrets/tapo/credentials is wrong.

panels.title: Thermometer Last Heard
panels.description: Past 10 min the room readings drop out. Never heard: check `journalctl -u govee-exporter`, that it is in range, and that the phone app isn't connected to it (it stops advertising while it is).

panels.title: Thermometer Battery
panels.description: Two AAA cells.
